lectures.title: The States: Governor and Chief Minister

parts.t: Governor and Chief Minister: who is who
items: **Governor:** Head of the State; the Nominal / Constitutional Head of the State.
**Chief Minister:** Head of the Government; the Real Executive Head of the State (the real executive is the Chief Minister + Council of Ministers).
**Chief Minister:** Head of the State Council of Ministers.
**Chief Minister:** Leader of the majority party/coalition in the State Legislative Assembly.
**Governor is not elected:** he is nominated/appointed.
**Article 153:** There shall be a Governor for each State. The same person can be appointed as Governor of two or more States (7th Amendment).
**Article 154:** Executive power of the State is vested in the Governor.
**Appointment (Art. 155):** Appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
**Tenure (Art. 156):** Holds office during the pleasure of the President, not the Chief Minister.
**Normal term:** 5 years (can be removed earlier or continue longer); continues until successor assumes office.
**Removal:** Removed by the President at pleasure (Art. 156); no impeachment.
**Resignation (Art. 156(2)):** Addressed to the President of India.
**3.** Should not be a member of Parliament or State Legislature (if he is, he must vacate the seat).
**4.** Should not hold any office of profit.
**Oath (Art. 159):** Administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court (or senior-most HC Judge).
**Governor:** Oath by the Chief Justice of the State High Court, but resigns to the President of India (Art. 156(2)).

**Article 158 & 202(3):** Emoluments of Governor and items charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State; the Governor's emoluments and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State (Art. 202).

**Dual-State Governor (Art. 158(3A)):** When the same individual is appointed Governor of two or more (≥ 2) States, the emoluments and allowances payable are allocated among the States in such proportion as the President may by order determine.
**Ministers:** Appoints the Chief Minister and other Ministers (on advice of CM).
**Other appointments:** Appoints Advocate-General, State Election Commissioner, Chairman & members of SPSC, etc.
**Information (Art. 167):** Can seek information from the Chief Minister.
**President's Rule:** Can recommend President's Rule under Article 356.
**Contingency Fund of the State:** operated by the Governor.
**Art. 168:** Integral part of the State Legislature.
**Sessions:** Summons, prorogues and dissolves the Legislative Assembly.
**Legislative Council:** Nominates members to the Legislative Council (if the State has one): 1/6th of total strength.

**Disqualification of MLAs:** on the ground of defection (Anti-Defection) it is decided by the Speaker of the Assembly; other disqualification questions are decided by the Governor on the opinion of the Election Commission.
**Options on a Bill:** Governor can give assent, withhold assent, return an ordinary Bill (no fixed time limit), or reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President.
**Reservation is discretionary:** Can reserve a Bill for the President even if the Council of Ministers advises otherwise.
**Ordinance power:** Promulgates Ordinances when the Legislature is not in session (during legislative recess).
**Life of an Ordinance:** ceases to operate 6 weeks after the reassembly of the State Legislature unless approved earlier.
**Governor's ordinance** requires approval by the State Legislature, NOT the Union Council of Ministers or the President.
**Pardoning power (Art. 161):** Power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, suspend or commute sentences, only for offences against State laws.
**District Judges:** Appoints District Judges (in consultation with High Court).
**Immunity (Article 361):** No criminal proceedings during term of office; civil proceedings only after 2 months' notice.

parts.t: Governor: discretionary powers and special provisions
items: **Not bound in all matters:** Not bound by the advice of Council of Ministers in all matters (has discretionary powers).
Appointment of **Chief Minister** in case of **hung Assembly**
**Dismissal of Council of Ministers** that has lost majority
**Reserving a Bill** for the consideration of the President
**Special responsibility** in certain States (e.g., Sixth Schedule areas, Tribal areas, etc.)
**Fifth Schedule:** Governor has special responsibility for Scheduled Areas. Submits report to the President.
**Sixth Schedule:** Special powers regarding Autonomous District Councils.
Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor
Other provisions as to Ministers: appointment, tenure, responsibility, size limit, etc.
Duties of Chief Minister as respects the furnishing of information to Governor
**Who:** Normally the leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly.
**Hung Assembly:** Governor has discretionary power in appointing CM.
**House:** Can be from Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council (if the state has one).
**Non-member:** Need not be a member of the State Legislature at the time of appointment (must become a member within 6 months).
**Non-member minister:** can hold office for a maximum of 6 consecutive months without getting elected.
**Other Ministers:** Governor appoints CM, but CM advises on the appointment of other Ministers.
**CM of Delhi / Puducherry:** Appointed by the President (Delhi: Art. 239AA; Puducherry: Government of Union Territories Act, 1963).

parts.t: Chief Minister: oath, resignation and removal
items: Governor of the State (Ministers route via CM)
Dismissed by Governor on CM's advice / loss of Assembly majority
**1. Head of Council of Ministers:** selects ministers, allocates portfolios, can recommend removal of any minister.

**2. Link between Governor and Council of Ministers (Art. 167):** Communicates all decisions of the CoM relating to the administration of the affairs of the State and proposals for legislation to the Governor.
**Art. 167 (contd.):** Furnishes information required by the Governor.
**Art. 167 (contd.):** Submits for the consideration of the CoM any matter on which a decision has been taken by a Minister but which has not been considered by the Council.
**4. Chief Spokesperson** of the State Government.
**5. Advises the Governor on:** Appointment of other Ministers; Summoning & prorogation of the State Legislature; Dissolution of the Legislative Assembly.

parts.t: Council of Ministers: responsibility and size
items: **Collective Responsibility (Art. 164(2)):** Council of Ministers (including CM) is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.
**Only to the Assembly:** CM is responsible only to the Legislative Assembly (not to the Legislative Council).
**No-Confidence Motion:** If passed, the entire Council (including CM) must resign.
**15% ceiling (91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003; Art. 164(1A)):** Total Ministers (including CM) shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
**Minimum floor:** 12 Ministers (including CM); minimum strength in smaller states.
**First woman Chief Minister** of any State
**Sadr-e-Riyasat:** Governor of J&K was earlier called Sadr-e-Riyasat (changed to Governor in 1965).

corrections.title: The States: Governor and Chief Minister
corrections.rocket: First woman Governor of an independent State → Padmaja Naidu (West Bengal)
corrections.corrected: First woman Governor of West Bengal: Padmaja Naidu
corrections.checked: Rocket itself gives Sarojini Naidu (Uttar Pradesh, 1947) as the first woman Governor of any State, which was already in independent India; Padmaja Naidu (Governor 1956-67) was the first woman Governor of West Bengal (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmaja_Naidu; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_India)

corrections.title: The States: Governor and Chief Minister
corrections.rocket: Decision on disqualification of MLAs under Anti-Defection → Governor (on advice of Election Commission).
corrections.corrected: Disqualification of MLAs: on the ground of defection (Anti-Defection) it is decided by the Speaker of the Assembly; other disqualification questions are decided by the Governor on the opinion of the Election Commission.
corrections.checked: Tenth Schedule para 6: questions of disqualification on ground of defection are referred to the Chairman/Speaker of the House; Article 192: the Governor decides other disqualification questions (Art. 191(1)) after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission (Constitution text, https://mea.gov.in/Images/pdf1/S10.pdf)

corrections.title: The States: Governor and Chief Minister
corrections.rocket: CM of Delhi / Puducherry | Appointed by the President (Art. 239AA)
corrections.corrected: CM of Delhi / Puducherry: Appointed by the President (Delhi: Art. 239AA; Puducherry: Government of Union Territories Act, 1963).
corrections.checked: Art. 239AA applies only to the NCT of Delhi; Puducherry's legislature and Council of Ministers rest on Art. 239A and the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, under which the President appoints the CM (https://www.mea.gov.in/Images/pdf1/Part8.pdf; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Puducherry)
